core_meaning.short_meaning: Prominent, distinguished leader; Badri companion Kharijah ibn Zayd al-Ansari.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Kharijah (خَارِجَة) is a historic Arabic masculine given name meaning 'prominent leader', 'one who emerges distinguished', or 'preeminent champion'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Kharijah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, chieftain of the Khazraj who pledged allegiance at the Second Pledge of Aqaba, fought at Badr, and was paired by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as the brother of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Active participle signifying one who stands out prominently in excellence, valor, and conspicuous virtue.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root kh-r-j signifies emerging into the open, excelling, and prominence. Kharijah ibn Zayd was one of the Medinan chieftains who welcomed the Prophet ﷺ. When the Prophet established the brotherhood (Mu'akhah) between the Emigrants and Helpers, he paired his closest companion, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, with Kharijah. At the Battle of Uhud, Kharijah fought with extraordinary bravery until he attained martyrdom, receiving over ten mortal wounds defending the Prophet.
